scientific_state: accepted finite descriptive result with explicit prediction dispositions
finding: Can acquisition route predict a choice after need satisfaction? The two-route reader beats both single-route assumptions on post-devaluation choice loss in every tested condition. Under broken contingency its loss is 0.456 nats, versus 0.926 for the model-based-only reader and 1.212 for association-only. Yet observational aliases keep route probability exactly at one half. This is a constructed-mechanism prediction result, not proof that the historical route is always identifiable.
